question.worked_solution:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ as follows: 

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-1,1)}\frac{{x}^{2}+2xy+{y}^{2}}{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}=\frac{(-1)^{2}+2\cdot (-1)\cdot 1+{1}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-(-1)^{2}}=\frac{0}{0}
$$

However, we can simplify the limit by canceling common factors in the numerator and denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1,1)}\frac{{x}^{2}+2xy+{y}^{2}}{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}} & ={lim}_{x\to (-1,1)}\frac{(x+y)^{2}}{(y-x)(y+x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (-1,1)}\frac{(x+y)(x+y)}{(y-x)(x+y)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (-1,1)}\frac{x+y}{y-x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it using direct substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (-1,1)}\frac{x+y}{y-x} & =\frac{(-1)+1}{1-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{0}{2} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $0.$
